summary.en: Sixty-two treasure ships and 27,800 men, plus horse transports, grain ships, water ships and warships.

description.zh: 《明史·郑和传》记「造大舶，修四十四丈、广十八丈者六十二」，将士二万七千八百余人。船队按职能分宝船、马船、粮船、水船、战船，另有通事、火长、医官与匠人。宝船尺度的折算历来有争议，此处按《明史》记录并注明「一说」。
description.en: The History of Ming records 62 great ships of 44 zhang by 18 zhang and 27,800 men. The fleet was organised by function into treasure ships, horse transports, grain ships, water ships and warships, with interpreters, navigators, physicians and craftsmen. The metric conversion of the treasure-ship dimensions is disputed; the History of Ming figures are given here with that caveat.

description.en: The fleet carried bolts of brocade and gauze, porcelain, ironware and copper cash, along with umbrellas, glass beads and combs — for gifts to rulers and for market exchange alike. The return cargo was spices, gems and exotic animals.

summary.zh: 船队以水罗盘定针路，昼夜兼行。
summary.en: The fleet steered by water compass along recorded compass courses.

description.zh: 明代航海以水罗盘（指南浮针）配合「针路」簿，记录各港口之间的罗经方位与更数（航程单位）。《郑和航海图》即以此体系绘成，是船队能够在无地标的远洋保持航向的基础。
description.en: Ming navigation used a floating-needle compass together with written sailing directions recording the bearing and the number of watches between ports. The Zheng He Nautical Chart was drawn in exactly this system, and it is what allowed the fleet to hold a course out of sight of land.

summary.en: The fleet carried great quantities of Yongle cash, which circulated across Southeast Asia and the Indian Ocean.

summary.en: The fleet sails south from Liujiagang and anchors at Taiping Port in Changle to refit and wait for the north-east monsoon, then puts out through the Wuhu Gate.

description.zh: 郑和船队沿海南下，在长乐太平港驻泊数月，修补船具、补充给养，等待冬季东北季风。此后船队自闽江口五虎门扬帆，经台湾海峡南下。
description.en: The fleet moved down the coast and lay at Taiping Port for several months, repairing gear and taking on supplies while waiting for the winter north-east monsoon. It then sailed out through the Wuhu Gate at the mouth of the Min River and headed south through the Taiwan Strait.

summary.en: On the Indian Ocean crossing the fleet measured the altitude of Polaris with star boards to fix latitude.

description.zh: 「过洋牵星」用十二块牵星板测星体出水高度，换算出南北位置，与罗盘针路互补。《郑和航海图》在孟加拉湾与阿拉伯海航段逐段标注「指某星若干指」，即牵星数据。
description.en: The technique used a set of twelve star boards to measure the altitude of a star above the horizon and convert it into a north–south position, complementing the compass course. The Nautical Chart annotates the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea legs with star altitudes.

summary.en: Zheng He invests Parameswara as king of Malacca, granting him a silver seal, robes and belt.

description.en: Malacca controlled the Strait of Malacca and sought Ming protection against Siam. Zheng He invested its chief Parameswara as king, granting a silver seal, robes, belt and brocade; Malacca became the fleet’s most important base in the western ocean.

description.en: Palembang, the old centre of Srivijaya, was held by the Guangdong-born pirate Chen Zuyi, who preyed on passing traders. Zheng He opened with diplomacy and sent envoys to summon him; Chen feigned surrender while preparing an ambush, setting the stage for the battle of 1407.

description.en: While the fleet was trading ashore in Java, the civil war between the eastern and western kings of Majapahit led the western king’s troops to kill 170 Ming soldiers by mistake. Fearing retribution, the king sent envoys to apologize and offered gold; Zheng He put the wider interests of trade first and did not retaliate.

summary.zh: 回程再至锡兰山，亚烈苦奈儿诱郑和入国并发兵五万围攻船队；郑和率两千人夜袭王城，生擒亚烈苦奈儿及其家属。
summary.en: On the return leg Alakeshvara lures Zheng He inland and sends 50,000 men against the fleet; Zheng He storms the capital by night with 2,000 men and captures the king and his family.

description.zh: 郑和回程再访锡兰山，亚烈苦奈儿诱其入国、索要财物，被拒后发兵五万围攻船队，并伐木阻断归路。郑和趁其国中空虚，率随从两千人取小道夜袭王城，破城擒王。永乐九年六月船队还朝，献俘于朝。
description.en: On the return the fleet called at Ceylon again. Alakeshvara lured Zheng He inland and demanded treasure; when refused he sent 50,000 men to surround the fleet and felled trees to cut off its retreat. With the capital stripped of defenders, Zheng He led 2,000 men by a side path in a night assault, took the city and captured the king and his household. The fleet returned to court in the sixth month of 1411 with the captives.

Afterwards, it was said, the overseas states stood in greater awe of the Ming court’s virtue.

summary.en: The sixth voyage carried home the envoys of sixteen states — diplomacy and escort in one.

summary.zh: 朝贡以「勘合」验真，回赐常倍于贡物，形成制度化的官方贸易。
summary.en: Tribute was verified by tallies, and return gifts often exceeded the tribute — institutionalised official trade.

description.zh: 明廷向海外诸国颁发勘合，贡使持勘合比对，以防伪冒。贡物入官，回赐以丝帛、瓷器、钱钞，价值常高于贡物。其实质是以国家财政支撑的官方贸易，也是下西洋难以长期维系的原因之一。
description.en: The Ming court issued tallies to foreign states; envoys presented the matching half on arrival to prevent imposture. Tribute entered the treasury, and return gifts of silk, porcelain and cash usually exceeded its value — official trade underwritten by the state, and one reason the voyages were hard to sustain.

name.en: The dimensions of the treasure ships

summary.zh: 宝船「修四十四丈、广十八丈」，尺度之说聚讼未决。
summary.en: The treasure ships are recorded as 44 zhang long and 18 zhang wide; the figure remains disputed.

description.zh: 《明史·郑和传》记宝船长四十四丈四尺、宽十八丈。按明尺折算约长 130 米，远超同期欧洲船只，因此有学者主张尺制或记载有误，一说为「五千料」巨舶。南京宝船厂遗址发现的大型作塘，可容此类船体建造。
description.en: The History of Ming gives the treasure ships as 44.4 zhang long and 18 zhang wide — roughly 130 m, far larger than any contemporary European vessel. Some scholars therefore argue the unit or the record is corrupt; another reading is a 5,000-liao ship. The large slipways excavated at the Nanjing treasure-ship yard could accommodate hulls of this scale.

description.en: Preserved in Mao Yuanyi’s Wubeizhi (1621), the chart runs to twenty pages and forty panels with more than 500 place names, from the Nanjing shipyard through Southeast Asia, India and Arabia to East Africa. description.zh: 宣德六年二月，宣宗因满剌加国王欲亲赴明朝朝贡而被暹罗阻拦，命郑和前往暹罗传谕，要求其与邻国和好、不得阻挠朝贡。
description.en: In the second month of 1431, because Siam had blocked the king of Malacca from coming to pay tribute, the Xuande Emperor ordered Zheng He to carry an edict to Siam demanding good relations with its neighbours and an end to interference with tribute missions.

summary.en: Zheng He rebuilds the Tianfei temple at Changle and sets up the “Tianfei Lingying” stele recording the voyages and the goddess’s protection.

description.zh: 船队在长乐候风期间重修天妃宫，立《天妃灵应之记》碑，碑文记述历次下西洋的时间和主要经历，是研究郑和航海的重要实物史料。
description.en: While waiting at Changle the fleet rebuilt the temple of the sea goddess Tianfei and erected the “Tianfei Lingying” stele. Its text records the dates and main events of the voyages and remains a key contemporary source for Zheng He’s navigation.

summary.en: The fleet reaches the Palembang commission and reassures the local Chinese leaders.

description.zh: 旧港在第一次下西洋后设宣慰司，以华侨施进卿为宣慰使。船队此次南巡，抚谕当地头目，重申明朝的羁縻统治。
description.en: After the first voyage a pacification commission had been set up at Palembang under the Chinese settler Shi Jinqing. On this voyage the fleet visited again, reassuring local leaders and restating Ming suzerainty.

summary.zh: 船队访问爪哇，与满者伯夷王廷通好。
summary.en: The fleet visits Java and opens friendly relations with the Majapahit court.

description.zh: 爪哇是南洋人口最稠密、物产最丰富的地区之一。船队在此交易香料、蔗糖与布匹，并与满者伯夷王廷通好。
description.en: Java was among the most populous and productive regions of the southern seas. The fleet traded for spices, sugar and cloth and established friendly relations with the Majapahit court.

summary.en: The fleet anchors at Malacca, reaffirms its enfeoffment and waits while squadrons form.

description.zh: 满剌加是船队在西洋的中转基地。郑和在此重申明朝对满剌加的册封与保护，并安排前往天方与东非的航程。
description.en: Malacca was the fleet’s base in the western ocean. Zheng He reaffirmed Ming enfeoffment and protection and arranged the runs to Mecca and East Africa.

summary.en: At Calicut Zheng He sends envoys on to Mecca.

description.zh: 古里是第七次下西洋的西行枢纽。郑和在此分遣使者，随当地商船前往天方（麦加）朝觐并采办方物；主队则继续前往忽鲁谟斯、阿丹。
description.en: Calicut was the hinge of the seventh voyage’s westward run. Zheng He sent envoys on local ships to Mecca to perform the pilgrimage and obtain exotic goods, while the main fleet continued to Hormuz and Aden.

summary.en: The fleet reaches Hormuz, bestows gifts on the king and buys gems, spices and horses.

description.en: Hormuz was the trading hub at the mouth of the Persian Gulf. Zheng He distributed brocade, bought gems, pearls, spices and fine horses, and returned the Hormuz envoys.

summary.en: The fleet reaches Aden, rejoins the envoys returning from Mecca and buys frankincense, myrrh and gems.

description.en: Aden guarded the mouth of the Red Sea. The fleet bought frankincense, myrrh, gems and spices there, rejoined the envoys returning from Mecca, and then sailed south to East Africa.

summary.en: A detachment of Zheng He’s fleet visited Mecca for pilgrimage and trade.

description.zh: 郑和在古里分遣使者，随当地商船前往天方（麦加）朝觐，并采办麒麟、狮子、鸵鸟等方物。使者往返历时数月，其后在阿丹与主队会合。
description.en: At Calicut Zheng He sent envoys on local ships to Mecca to perform the pilgrimage and obtain qilin, lions, ostriches and other exotic goods. The round trip took several months, and the envoys rejoined the fleet at Aden.

summary.en: The fleet sails south to Mogadishu to exchange for ivory, spices and local products.

description.zh: 木骨都束是东非航线的重要停靠点。船队在此以瓷器、丝绸交换象牙、香料与牲畜，并补充淡水。
description.en: Mogadishu was a key stop on the East African run. The fleet exchanged porcelain and silk for ivory, spices and livestock, and took on fresh water.

summary.en: Zheng He dies at Calicut during the seventh voyage.

description.zh: 1433 年，郑和在第七次下西洋归程中病逝于古里，终年六十余岁。船队由太监王景弘等率领，于是年七月返抵南京。
description.en: In 1433, on the return leg of the seventh voyage, Zheng He died at Calicut in his sixties. The fleet returned to Nanjing in the seventh month under the eunuch Wang Jinghong and others.

summary.zh: 返航载回香料、宝石、珍禽与各国贡物。
summary.en: The fleet returned with spices, gems, exotic animals and tribute goods.

description.zh: 回程货物以胡椒、苏木、沉香、乳香、没药、宝石、珍珠、象牙、犀角为主，另有麒麟、狮子、鸵鸟等。香料一项后来成为明廷财政与民间市场的大宗，也改变了中国人的饮食与医药。
description.en: The return cargo was dominated by pepper, sappanwood, aloeswood, frankincense, myrrh, gems, pearls, ivory and rhinoceros horn, besides giraffes, lions and ostriches. Spices in particular became a major item in court revenue and in ordinary markets, changing Chinese cooking and pharmacy.
